raw_response:
I would keep this year simple and familiar. In Quzhou County, the safest way for me to make use of the land and water is the usual winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. That matches the local climate, the irrigation setup, and the work rhythm I already know. Because I am 59 and I have no reason to chase a risky crop, I would put almost all my land into the wheat-maize rotation and keep only a small piece for peanuts to bring in some cash and spread a little risk. For wheat, I would stay with an improved variety instead of a hybrid, use moderate fertilizer, irrigate at the key stages, and spray only when disease or insects really show up. After wheat harvest, I would move quickly into hybrid summer maize, because maize gives stable yield here and fits well after wheat. On the peanut plot, I would keep inputs lower than maize, use rotary tillage, watch weeds and leaf disease, and avoid overwatering. My goal would be steady production, manageable labor, and lower risk rather than trying something new.
